- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day peaks) — cap forecast at 2x recent high or 1.5x prior 30d mean to avoid overshoot.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion — if recent 18d mean is >1.80, forecast should not exceed 2.20 unless sentiment is strong.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- When sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and history shows no clear trend, model underperforms — use 18d moving average as baseline for 30d forecast.
